skills.name: parametrize_plane_conics_as_projective_space
skills.description: Identify the set of plane conics with the projective space of homogeneous quadratic forms in three variables, i.e. \(\mathbb{P}^5\), by sending a conic to its coefficient vector up to scaling.
skills.preconditions: A projective plane \(\mathbb{P}^2\) over a field and the line bundle \(\mathcal{O}(2)\).
skills.postconditions: A bijection between smooth conics and points of an open subset of \(\mathbb{P}^5\), providing coordinates for each conic.
skills.example: For \(\mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}\), the conic defined by \(x^2+yz=0\) corresponds to the point \([1:0:0:0:1:0]\) in \(\mathbb{P}^5\) given by the coefficients of \(x^2, xy, xz, y^2, yz, z^2\).

skills.name: express_tangency_condition_via_resultant
skills.description: Translate the condition that two plane conics are tangent into the vanishing of the resultant of their defining quadratic forms and a linear combination of their gradients, yielding a homogeneous polynomial equation in the coefficients.
skills.preconditions: Two conics given by homogeneous quadratic forms \(F,G\) in three variables.
skills.postconditions: An explicit polynomial equation \(T(F,G)=0\) whose vanishing is equivalent to \(F\) and \(G\) sharing a tangent line at some point.
skills.example: For conics \(F=x^2+y^2-z^2\) and \(G=xy-z^2\) in \(\mathbb{P}^2\), the tangency condition reduces to the vanishing of the determinant \(\det\begin{pmatrix} \partial F/\partial x & \partial F/\partial y & \partial F/\partial z \\ \partial G/\partial x & \partial G/\partial y & \partial G/\partial z \\ x & y & z \end{pmatrix}=0\).

skills.name: set_up_incidence_correspondence_and_compute_dimension
skills.description: Create an incidence variety pairing objects (e.g., a conic and a point of tangency) and use dimension counting to determine the expected dimension of the projection onto one factor.
skills.preconditions: A product space \(X\times Y\) where a closed condition \(Z\subset X\times Y\) is defined by polynomial equations.
skills.postconditions: The dimension of \(Z\) and of its image under projection are computed, indicating whether the projection is generically finite.
skills.example: For the set of pairs \((C,P)\) where \(C\) is a line in \(\mathbb{P}^2\) and \(P\) lies on \(C\), the incidence variety is a \(\mathbb{P}^1\)-bundle over \(\mathbb{P}^2\) of dimension 2, and its projection to the space of lines (\(\mathbb{P}^{2*}\)) is surjective with 1‑dimensional fibers.

skills.name: apply_bezout_theorem_to_intersection_of_hypersurfaces
skills.description: Use Bézout's theorem to compute the number of points in a zero‑dimensional complete intersection of hypersurfaces in projective space, assuming proper intersection.
skills.preconditions: A set of homogeneous polynomials \(f_1,\dots,f_r\) in \(\mathbb{P}^n\) whose common zero locus is zero‑dimensional and the hypersurfaces intersect transversely.
skills.postconditions: The total count (with multiplicities) of intersection points equals the product of the degrees \(\deg f_1\cdots\deg f_r\).
skills.example: In \(\mathbb{P}^3\), intersecting a quadric surface (degree 2) and a cubic surface (degree 3) that meet properly yields \(2\times3=6\) points counted with multiplicity.

skills.name: compute_degree_of_projection_map_using_generic_fiber
skills.description: Determine the degree of a dominant morphism by counting the number of points in a generic fiber, often via dimension arguments and intersection theory.
skills.preconditions: A dominant morphism \(\pi: X\to Y\) between irreducible varieties of the same dimension, with \(\pi\) finite over a dense open subset of \(Y\).
skills.postconditions: The integer \(\deg \pi\) equal to the cardinality of a generic fiber (counted with multiplicity).
skills.example: The map \(\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1\) given by \(t\mapsto t^3\) has degree 3 because a generic point \(y\) has three preimages \(\sqrt[3]{y}\).

skills.name: use_lang_weil_estimate_for_point_counts_over_finite_fields
skills.description: Apply the Lang–Weil estimate to bound the number of \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-rational points on a geometrically irreducible variety in terms of its dimension and degree.
skills.preconditions: A geometrically irreducible projective variety \(X\) of dimension \(d\) and degree \(\delta\) defined over \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
skills.postconditions: An estimate \(|\#X(\mathbb{F}_p)-p^d|\le C\,p^{d-1/2}\) for some constant \(C\) depending only on \(d\) and \(\delta\).
skills.example: For a smooth plane cubic curve (dimension 1, degree 3) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\), Lang–Weil gives \(|\#C(\mathbb{F}_p)-p|\le 2\sqrt{p}\).

skills.name: deduce_average_fiber_size_of_finite_etale_map_equals_degree
skills.description: Use the fact that for a finite étale morphism \(\pi: X\to Y\) over a finite field, the average size of the fibers over \(\mathbb{F}_p\)-points of \(Y\) tends to the degree of \(\pi\) as \(p\to\infty\).
skills.preconditions: A finite étale morphism \(\pi: X\to Y\) defined over \(\mathbb{F}_p\) with \(Y\) geometrically irreducible.
skills.example: For the covering \(\mathbb{A}^1\to\mathbb{A}^1\), \(t\mapsto t^2\), which is finite étale away from 0, the average number of square roots of a random element of \(\mathbb{F}_p\) approaches 2, the degree.

skills.name: apply_generic_smoothness_to_guarantee_etale_locus_dense_open
skills.description: Invoke generic smoothness to conclude that the set of points where a morphism is smooth (hence étale for finite maps) contains a dense open subset of the target.
skills.preconditions: A morphism \(f: X\to Y\) between varieties of finite type over a field of characteristic 0 (or large enough characteristic), with \(X\) reduced.
skills.postconditions: Existence of a dense open \(U\subset Y\) such that \(f\) is smooth (and therefore étale if also finite) over \(U\).
skills.example: The projection \(\pi: V\subset\mathbb{A}^3\to\mathbb{A}^2\) given by \((x,y,z)\mapsto (x,y)\) from the surface \(z^2=xy\) is smooth away from the origin, so the étale locus is \(\mathbb{A}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}\).

skills.name: use_dual_plane_and_dual_curve_to_translate_tangency_to_incidence
skills.description: Replace a tangency condition between a conic and a fixed conic by the incidence of a point in the dual plane lying on the dual curve of the fixed conic.
skills.preconditions: A plane curve \(C\subset\mathbb{P}^2\) and its projective dual \(C^*\subset(\mathbb{P}^2)^*\).
skills.postconditions: The set of conics tangent to \(C\) corresponds to points in \(\mathbb{P}^5\) whose associated dual line lies on \(C^*\), turning a quadratic tangency condition into a linear incidence in the dual space.
skills.example: For a smooth cubic curve \(E\) in \(\mathbb{P}^2\), a line \(L\) is tangent to \(E\) iff the point in the dual plane representing \(L\) lies on the dual cubic curve \(E^*\).

skills.name: evaluate_degree_via_chern_classes_and_intersection_numbers
skills.description: Compute the degree of a morphism or the class of a subvariety by expressing it as an intersection product of Chern classes in the Chow ring of a projective space.
skills.preconditions: A vector bundle \(E\) over a smooth projective variety \(X\) and a section whose zero locus defines the subvariety of interest.
skills.postconditions: The degree (or class) equals the top Chern class \(c_{\text{top}}(E)\) evaluated on \([X]\), giving a concrete integer via standard intersection formulas.
skills.example: The number of lines on a smooth cubic surface is computed by intersecting the class \(c_2(T_{\mathbb{P}^3})\) with the class of the cubic, yielding \(27\).
